Extra-Curricular Enrichment Clubs
At Sulhamstead and Ufton Nervet Primary School, our enrichment clubs play an important role in enhancing the school experience for all children. We are proud to offer a range of opportunities that allow pupils to explore new interests, develop existing talents and build confidence in a supportive and inclusive environment.
Our clubs are designed to complement the curriculum while promoting creativity, teamwork, wellbeing and enjoyment. We value pupil voice and aim to provide a variety of activities that reflect the interests of our children.
Some of the clubs we currently offer include:
Our enrichment clubs are led by dedicated staff and experienced external providers. They offer valuable opportunities for children to try something new, form friendships across year groups and develop skills beyond the classroom.
Current Clubs Timetable
We continually review and adapt our club offer to ensure it remains engaging, inclusive and responsive to the needs and interests of our pupils.
Mondays 8.30am - Year 1-6 iRock. Visit http://www.irockschool.com/ for more information
Mondays 3.15 - 4.15 - Year 1-6 Yoga Club
Tuesdays 12.15 - 12.45 - Year 1-6 Stageability Drama Club
Tuesdays 3.15-4.30pm - Years 1-6 Explorers Club run jointly by the school and the Church. Please contact the school office to enquire about spaces.
Thursday 3.15-4.15pm - MNR Football Club. Please book via the School Gateway app.
Fridays Lego Club (Half Termly Dates TBC - please check the School Calendar)
For 1:1 musical instrument lessons please contact Berkshire Music Trust directly.

Explorers Club
Explorers is a jointly run afterschool club here at SUN school with friends from our Church, St Marys Sulhamstead and from school.
It was started about 25 years ago by a teacher at the school and a couple of parents from the church. The aim was to explore the Christian faith in a fun and exciting way and to foster links between the school and the church. And it is still running with those aims today. The club is open to all children from SUN school from Year 1 to Year 6. It has been encouraging to see many of our old pupils going along to the Christian Union at The Willink, our main feeder secondary school. Here the Christian faith is explored and discussed along side eating cake! All children from Explorers and the school along with their families are always very welcome at the services at St Marys. Explorers are invited to take part in special services from time to time at church.
A typical session starts with a drink and a snack and a chance to relax after a busy day at school. We then play some games outside with Hide and Seek being all the time favourite. We explore a story from the bible and there is usually a craft or activity linked to this. We end our time together with a short reflection that includes a song and a prayer.
In recent times we have made prayer boxes for each classes worship area. The boxes contain crosses, candles, and different coloured drapes to reflect the colours of the church year. As well we made scrap books of the bible stories that accompany the School Values. We appreciated the help with the coloured cloth from friends at the church.
We spent a year doing a Bible overview from cover to cover using The Block Buster Bible. This book takes a look behind the scenes of the bible and uses the theme of films. Each week the children acted out the story using the clapper board and shouting Lights, Camera Action! We were thrilled to have the author Andrew Pritchard come and talk to us!
This school year we are exploring the Christian values of the school. We have just finishing considering how to be thankful and have been out and about in the school grounds.

Parent Learning Resources
Please see resources below that will help you support your child in key areas of learning at home.
Reading
What can you do to help?
As always, we recommend you spend as much time reading as possible! Now, more than ever, reading is a great escape into different stories to explore. Below are a few suggestions of websites and resources that you can use to help your child to develop and grow as a reader.
Here is the link to a reading list for Key Stage 2 pupils - it is helpful for new ideas and books for your child.
https://schoolreadinglist.co.uk/reading-lists-for-ks2-school-pupils/
Audible have made a selection of titles free to use for children on desktops, laptops, tablets or phones. Lots of great stories to explore here.
https://stories.audible.com/start-listen
TheSchoolRun.com is a good website to have a look at for learning ideas. There is some downloadable content you might want to explore linked to grammar and literacy alongside other curriculum areas. They have phonics, spelling, handwriting, grammar and reading comprehension support available on their website.
https://www.theschoolrun.com/

As educators, we understand that learning is about so much more than reading and writing. Therefore, alongside the subject based national curriculum and our commitment to help our children develop strategies for positive mental well-being, we have developed a Life Skills curriculum.
At Sulhamstead and Ufton Nervet Primary School, our Life Skills curriculum is designed to give the children the knowledge, skills, language, tools and cultural currency to navigate successfully from childhood through to adult life. We will achieve this through a bespoke programme of lessons - designed to meet the needs of our pupils, both within school and the wider community. Our lessons will allow the children to express their honest thoughts and feelings in a safe, informed and mutually respectful environment. We dedicate a session a week to Life Skills and Well-being/Mindfulness as part of our broad and balanced curriculum.
Our Life Skills curriculum aims to ensure that all our children flourish; we want them to thrive, not just survive. We want our pupils to leave us with a strong moral and practical foundation, ready to embrace the opportunities and challenges of modern life with confidence and ambition.

Attendance
Attendance and Punctuality
Attendance
At Sulhamstead & Ufton Nervet CE Primary School, we believe that attendance and punctuality are important disciplines that help to structure our daily lives and must be modelled and taught to the children. Schools have a duty to prepare pupils for life in the 21st century as responsible members of our community and part of this journey is to teach them about the importance of attendance and punctuality.
As a school, we monitor attendance closely, so please do inform school if there are significant issues impacting your child that mean that your child may not meet the National Expectation of 96% attendance. Do ensure you speak to your child’s teacher or Miss Kennedy, as we will always try to support you and your child.
Punctuality
Our school day starts when the doors open at 8.35 giving plenty of time for children to come into school and be ready for learning to start at 8.45. We have Morning Challenges in class that are designed to prime the children’s brains ready for learning, and these start as soon as the children enter the classroom. If a child consistently misses, even these first ten minutes of the school day, that means that the equivalent of one whole 50 minute lesson a week is missed.
Over a year that equates to 15 hours of learning time lost!
Over time this can have a significant impact on your child’s learning.
At SUN, we treasure all learning time in class, and want to support you and your children to get the most out of the school day. If you are encountering any problems around ensuring your child can arrive on time, please do come and speak to your class teacher or Miss Kennedy. By informing the school, we can give you as much support as possible.
One way we help families in the mornings is for them to attend our Funtastic Kids Breakfast Club. Do consider this as an option if you feel it will help.
Thank you for your continued support to ensure all of our children are making the most of their school day.
Sickness and Absence
Parents should inform the School Office if their child is sick and therefore going to be absent from school before 9.15am. For certain types of illness, the School Office will give advice, based on Public Health England guidance, in relation to when your child should return to school (see below).
https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/is-my-child-too-ill-for-school/
Diarrhoea and Vomiting
Primary schools typically have a ‘48 hour rule’ in relation to diarrhoea and vomiting. In that respect, they are simply following NHS guidelines and Public Health England Guidance 2016, which recommends that children should be kept away from school, nursery for 48 hours ‘from their last episode of diarrhoea or vomiting.’ (Guidance on Infection Control in Schools and other Childcare Settings 2016, p6) and earlier guidance from the NHS and Public Health England.
Public Health England Guidance
Leave of Absence Requests
Education is a once in a lifetime opportunity and holidays should not be taken during term time.
Headteachers are only be able to grant a leave of absence during term time in exceptional circumstances - taking your child out of school during term time without specific permission will lead to legal action, including fines.
Holidays in term time have a serious detrimental impact on a student’s education and can be damaging to an individual’s development in school and educational chances.
Holidays in term time are not seen as a 'right' and therefore will not automatically be granted.
Any absence taken where a request has been refused by the Headteacher, the absence will be recorded as “Unauthorised Absence”. Such unauthorised holiday absence will result in a fixed penalty fine and legal action through a Magistrate’s court. Fixed Penalty Fines are issued per parent per child.
You are advised not to make any booking before ascertaining if the proposed holiday can be authorised.

Friends of SUN
We are very fortunate at our school to have a Friends’ Association that has always been such an integral part of the school community for many years. In its time the Friends of SUN has raised many thousands of pounds, which have been spent on improving equipment and resources to enhance our children’s education and the facilities in school.
But it is much more than just fundraising. The Friends of SUN Association, or FoS for short, also exists to provide closer links between home and school, and it is an excellent way to bring staff, parents and pupils together in support of the school to work towards common goals.
It is challenging to organise bigger event, but with the continued support of parents and staff, we have always succeeded in our efforts, just ask any of the committee or parent helpers how rewarding and fun it can be!
All parents and members of the school community can be involved, even if you only have a small amount of time available; all parents automatically become members of the Friends of SUN when their child gets a place in our school.
FoS are conscious of the ethos and values of our school, and we try very hard to respect this when organising and planning events to ensure a variety of activities with something for everyone.
Our FoS Committee currently consists of 2 Officers (Chair, Treasurer) along with several other Committee members to make up the full Committee who are trustees for the charity.
Our Committee for 2025/2026
Treasurer: Julie Mackowan Farmer

How We Spend The Money We Raise
The money we raise is usually spent fairly quickly - this way, parents can be sure that in supporting our school, all children will benefit from our fundraising efforts.
Usually our Headteacher has a ‘wish list’ of items that the school would like to purchase. Often for resources to improve a particular area of the curriculum or school environment. Sometimes this will be as a result of the children or parents asking for something in particular.
Friends’ funds are not spent on improving the fabric of the school building as this is the responsibility of the school’s Governing Board. Our Constitution commits us to spending money on things that will benefit the children directly. It states that funds are to be used to “provide facilities or equipment which support the school and advance the education of the pupils” and that we also aim to achieve this by “engaging in activities” and “developing effective relationships between the staff, parents and others associated with the school”
Here are just some of the things that the Friends have helped to raise money for:
Educational activities
Subsidising school trips, such as whole school trip to Christmas Pantos, class tips to museums and educational centres, visiting theatre performers and inspirating visitors;
Subscriptions for the children to use such as TTRS/Numbots, MyMaths and SpellingShed;
Previous years we have paid for resources and visitors for an off-timetable Science Week or Arts Week; Yoga and a climbing wall for our Wellbeing Week, coaches for the Sports week;
At times we have paid for prizes, keepsakes, ice creams, Easter eggs and Yr 6 Hoodies;
Equipment for Classrooms, books for the library, tablet covers, smart boards, cooking equipment and ingredients;
A brand new Reading Scheme with books for the whole school;
Resources, including playground and indoor play equipment, outdoor games, playground markings, staging, storage units, picnic benches and sun shades.
In the main, Friends’ funds are for the ‘extras’ not provided by the school budget, that make our children’s learning experiences even more fulfilling and exciting.
How You Can Get Involved
There are ways you can help and support your child through FoS:
You can start to help us fundraise by doing you online shopping through EasyFundraising (see link below), where “Friends of SUN—Reading” receive a donation at no cost to you. 50% of funds go to the charity you have chosen to support and 10% is split between varying West Berkshire charities.
